# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one spinner chain and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage` and `internal/ui/datatable` |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one spinner chain and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage` and `internal/ui/datatable` |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

Tu rédiges la documentation destinée aux lecteurs du produit (utilisateurs et développeurs).

## Méthode

1. Identifie le lecteur et ce qu'il veut accomplir.
2. Vérifie chaque commande, chemin et exemple dans le code ou en l'exécutant ;

3. Mets à jour la documentation existante avant d'en créer de nouvelle.
4. Structure : but, prérequis, étapes, exemple, dépannage.

## Style

Phrases courtes, voix active, un exemple exécutable par concept. Reprends la langue
et le ton de la documentation déjà présente dans le projet.

## Hors périmètre

Décisions et `CLAUDE.md` → `archivist`. Changelog et notes de version → `devops`.

Si une information qui change le résultat manque ou est ambiguë (public visé, comportement réel d'une commande, prérequis), ne la devine
pas : arrête-toi et rends tes questions en tête de ta sortie, sous **Questions
bloquantes**, chacune avec les options possibles et ta recommandation. L'orchestrateur
les posera à l'utilisateur. Pour un détail sans conséquence, choisis l'option la plus
prudente et signale-la dans ta sortie (`Hypothèse : …`).

**The animation travels in `jobs.FrameMsg`, to the view on screen only.** It
carries `Frame` (bare, Rule 122: a table cell is measured before it is styled),
`RenderedFrame` (styled, Rule 128: what a footer takes) and `Blink` (true is the
"on" half). Only the router builds one (`frameMsg`, in `internal/app/animation.go`).
Before DEVDESK-139 the frame rode in `ChangedMsg` and every tick made every held
view rebuild its rows; now a tick touches one view. `enterView` (snapshot plus
current frame) is called wherever a view takes the screen: `switchView`,
`openBrowser`, the path picker, `openSecurityView`, `rescanInOrigin` and
`returnToOrigin`. Without it a view would show the previous frame, or an "off"
phase, until the next tick.

#### One tick, one chain

There is **one** animation chain for the whole application (D5, renamed
"animation" by D2; it used to be the spinner chain): `animationTickMsg{seq, at}`,
started only by `ensureTick`, renewed only by `handleAnimationTick`
(`TestTheRouterHasOneAnimationChain` enforces both). It is built on `tea.Every`,
so ticks land on the clock's boundaries and the blink alternates strictly.

`App.Update` is a thin wrapper: it runs `update` (the dispatch), then
`ensureTick`. The check is a **level**, not an edge — it runs after every
message, so no handler has to remember to start a chain, and it is idempotent
within one `Update`.

| Need | Cadence |
|---|---|
| `jobs.Running() > 0` (footer spinners depend on the frame) | 100 ms (`spinner.Dot.FPS`) |
| the view on screen has nothing running but `WantsBlink()` (`BlinkingView`) | 500 ms |
| neither, or `motionStatic` with no running work | no chain |

`BlinkingView` sits beside `FormView` and `LeavingView`: an optional interface for
a row that blinks for a reason the registry does not know (an instant action, an
agent running, children loading). The router asks the view on screen after every
`Update`.

- **Seq.** A tick of a chain that was replaced is dropped without a Cmd, so a
  second chain is impossible rather than merely unlikely.
- **Faster need.** `ensureTick` replaces a slower live chain (`seq++`), never
  adds a second.
- **Slower need.** The live chain downgrades at its next renewal, without a new
  seq. When no cadence is wanted it is not renewed and dies.
- **Phase.** Read off the tick's own time, not a counter:
  `(t.UnixMilli()/500)%2 == 0` is on. Every view blinks in step whatever the
  interval the chain runs at (1 Hz).
- **Frame.** Advances only while `Running() > 0`.
- **At rest the phase is forced "on".** When the chain stops on an "off" phase,
  the router pins it on and sends one last `FrameMsg` to the view on screen: a
  settled row is left on a steady glyph, never a half-blinked one.
- **`motionStatic`.** Pins the phase on and keeps blink-only chains from
  starting (`setMotionStatic` hands the pinned frame to the view on screen at
  once). `app.motion` feeds `App.motionStatic` through `applyMotion`: at
  startup (`newWithSize`), after a context switch (`handleContextSwitchComplete`,
  once the views are rebuilt) and on `ConfigSavedMsg` (`handleConfigSaved`).

`jobsChanged` is what a launch site or a transition calls after writing to the
registry: `ChangedMsg` to every held view, `FrameMsg` to the view on screen. The
`Update` wrapper then makes sure a chain is alive; the three are separate, and
none implies another.

This is what removes the four hand-stamped frames, and with them the failure
each of them could produce: a chain that died on the first idle tick with
nothing able to restart it, leaving the spinner frozen on the frame it died at.

#### Row chains outside the router

No row-animation chain lives in a view: `TestNoRowAnimationChainOutsideTheRouter`
scans every source file outside `ui/datatable/` and fails on a row chain
(`AdvanceSpinner`, `portsSpinnerCmd`, a `tagScanSpinnerIdx` step), with no list
of declared chains to extend. `TestOnlyTheRouterBuildsAFrameMsg` and
`TestTheAnimationChainUnderARealProgram` (a real `tea.Program`, meant for
`-race`) complete the guard rails.

#### What the redraw costs

`DEVDESK_MEASURE_REDRAW=1 go test ./internal/app -run TestMeasureRedrawCost -v`
counts the bytes Bubble Tea's renderer writes to an `io.Writer` on a simulated
120x40 terminal — not a real terminal. Opt-in; the test is skipped otherwise.

| Animation | Bytes emitted |
|---|---|
| no animated row | 0 B/s |
| 1 row blinking at 1 Hz | 376 B/s |
| 20 rows blinking at 1 Hz | 5 809 B/s |
| reference: spinner at 10 Hz, 1 row | 1 880 B/s |
| reference: spinner at 10 Hz, 20 rows | 29 049 B/s |

Nothing animated costs nothing, and a 1 Hz blink costs about a fifth of the
10 Hz spinner it sits beside.


### The `:jobs` view — `internal/ui/jobsview`

The reader's side of the registry, and it owns nothing: it starts no work, holds
no timer and fetches nothing. Its rows are the snapshot, so there is nothing to
refresh — `ctrl+r` is absent rather than greyed, because there is no operation
behind it to be unavailable.

Two levels (D2): the runs, and `→` on one of them for its targets. A level
rather than a pair of tabs — the second table is *about* a row of the first, so
it is reached the way every drill-down in the application is (Rule 111), and the
trail is a breadcrumb below the table (Rule 123).

| | Columns |
|---|---|
| runs | activity indicator (untitled, `IconColumnWidth`), Kind, Label, Progress, State, Started |
| targets | activity indicator, Target, State, Detail |

**Column 0 is the activity indicator** (DEVDESK-142, Rule 125), built by
`datatable.IndicatorColumn` over `components.RunIndicator` / `ItemIndicator`
(`job_activity.go`): queued `◴`, running `●`/`○`, done `◉`, failed `⊗`,
cancelled `⊘`, skipped `⊖`. It is the state, not the kind: a jobs list is
scanned for the run that failed and the one still going. The Kind column
carries the state in its `Search` so `/failed` and `/scan` both work while the
glyph column stays out of the filter. The State word takes the dot's colour
(`indicator.Style`), so the row has one colour source; `done` is neutral, not
green, and queued, cancelled and skipped now share that neutral colour.

**The blink phase is read at render.** The rows carry nothing animated:
`runRow`/`itemRow` wrap the record only. `jobs.FrameMsg` calls
`SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` on both tables and pushes the footer spinner frame;
no row is rebuilt (`SetItems` stays the only way rows are rebuilt, from
`ChangedMsg`). A queued run no longer spins: it shows a fixed `◴`.

**The footer says the selected row.** `status()` fills `Status.Detail` with
`components.DescribeRun` (or `DescribeItem` at the target level) of the row
under the cursor, and keeps `N jobs running` as the text. The footer spinner is
shown only when no detail is, since the row's own dot moves. A `Warn` (a refused
`K` or `.`) keeps priority over the detail and the detail returns when it
expires. The help ends with `indicator.Legend(indicator.JobsLegend...)`.

**The context is passed, not read.** `jobsview.New(cfg, contextName)` takes the
name from the router, for D68's reason one screen over: the router is what knows
which context is current. The view filters the snapshot on it (`FilterContext`),
so a switch hides runs rather than dropping them — and the router rebuilds every
view on a switch anyway, so the cached name cannot go stale.

`K` is state-aware at both levels (Rule 130) and greyed with a **named** reason:
"This run has already finished", "A delete cannot be stopped once it has
started". The refusal is never silent — pressing a greyed key says why in the
footer.

**The dashboard gained the counter** the same way, and it is the one screen that
always gets D9's degraded form: it launches nothing, so it passes no origin, and
`2 jobs running — :jobs for details` is the whole of what it can honestly say.
The sentence itself is `components.JobsStatusLine`, shared with the workspaces
footer — two copies of a deliberate surrender would each have been free to
surrender differently.

### The activity-column guard (DEVDESK-142, A-16 skeleton)

`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go` keeps every view on the activity column
(Rule 125) and keeps it there. It classifies every `command.ViewType` into one of
two lists, **per table**: a view is migrated or exempt, never both and never
neither. There is no list of tables waiting for their story any more (DEVDESK-143
closed it) and no exception to shrink:

| List | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `migratedTables` | the view's tables are on the activity column (`:jobs`: `jobs/runs`, `jobs/targets`; ws: `ws`; `:sec`: `sec/inventory`; OCI: `oci/images`, `oci/networks`, `oci/volumes`, `oci/registries`, `oci/registry-browser`; explorer: `explorer/tree`, `explorer/clone-list`; templates: `templates`; netdiag: `netdiag/ports`; `:agent-usage`: `agent-usage/agents`; containers: `containers`) |
| `exemptViews` | views with no activity to show (dashboard, status, git-auth, configuration, about, files, viewer), each with its reason |

A view in neither list, or an exempt view that is also migrated, fails by name (`classificationProblems`, unit-tested on fictitious classifications). A migrated view
exposes `ActivityTables() map[string]datatable.ActivityTable` (a read-only face:
`Shapes()` and `RenderedWidth()`, see `ui-components.md`); an exempt view that reports any table fails with "remove the exception".

The netdiag view's `migratedSources` are two files only, `ports_model.go` and `ports_activity.go` (DEVDESK-150): netdiag migrates its Ports tab alone, and the guard scans the files that belong to it. `ports_commands.go` is left out: its `portsTickCmd` is the data refresh tick, not a row animation (same reasoning as OCI's `commands.go`). The other tabs (`forward_model.go`, checks, interfaces) are not migrated. It reports `netdiag/ports` from `ActivityTables()`, and its footer seed (`seedNetdiagFooter`) opens the Ports tab with one socket whose kill is in flight, driving the view's `Update` directly (no `Cmd` is run: no socket table read, no signal sent).

The `:agent-usage` view's `migratedSources` is the whole `ui/agentusageview/` package (no `tea.Tick` in it: `pollTickCmd` sleeps inside a `Cmd`), it reports `agent-usage/agents` from `ActivityTables()` and implements `WantsBlink()`; its footer seed (`seedAgentUsageFooter`) puts a transcript with a fresh line on disk and expects `indicator.Running`, without running the 2 s poll `Cmd`.

The templates view's `migratedSources` is the whole `ui/templates/` package; it reports `templates` from `ActivityTables()` and has a footer seed (a sync running on the selected row).

The explorer's `migratedSources` is the whole `explorer` package (no frame or `jobFrame` left in it). The explorer reports `explorer/clone-list` from `ActivityTables()` even with no clone running (same constructor), so the table is checked at 60 columns. The registry side adds `jobs.SafeCause` (credentials removed from a cause) and `jobs.CancelledDetail`.

**Checked at run time**, on each view built by the router: column 0 of every
migrated table is the indicator (untitled, fixed, `IconColumnWidth`, no `Less`,
no `Search`); `RenderedWidth()` equals `width-2` after a 60-column resize
(Rule 116); the help holds the `indicator.Legend` section.

**Checked by source analysis**, on migrated packages only (`ui/jobsview/`, `ui/workspaces/`, `ui/security/`): no
`AdvanceSpinner` call, no `StatusColumn:` key, no `Frame`/`frame`/`SpinnerFrame`
field or selector (`RenderedFrame` is allowed), no string or rune literal
holding an indicator glyph. Verified to fail on a positive case by injecting a `Frame`
field, an `AdvanceSpinner` call and a `"◉"` literal into `jobsview`.

**The footer half** is `migratedFooterSeeds` (a view seeds a row at a state and the
guard checks its footer): `:sec` is seeded by `seedSecurityFooter`, a running
scan on the selected row.

`SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` on both tables and pushes the footer spinner frame;
no row is rebuilt (`SetItems` stays the only way rows are rebuilt, from
`ChangedMsg`). A queued run no longer spins: it shows a fixed `◴`.

**The footer says the selected row.** `status()` fills `Status.Detail` with
`components.DescribeRun` (or `DescribeItem` at the target level) of the row
under the cursor, and keeps `N jobs running` as the text. The footer spinner is
shown only when no detail is, since the row's own dot moves. A `Warn` (a refused
`K` or `.`) keeps priority over the detail and the detail returns when it
expires. The help ends with `indicator.Legend(indicator.JobsLegend...)`.

**The context is passed, not read.** `jobsview.New(cfg, contextName)` takes the
name from the router, for D68's reason one screen over: the router is what knows
which context is current. The view filters the snapshot on it (`FilterContext`),
so a switch hides runs rather than dropping them — and the router rebuilds every
view on a switch anyway, so the cached name cannot go stale.

`K` is state-aware at both levels (Rule 130) and greyed with a **named** reason:
"This run has already finished", "A delete cannot be stopped once it has
started". The refusal is never silent — pressing a greyed key says why in the
footer.

**The dashboard gained the counter** the same way, and it is the one screen that
always gets D9's degraded form: it launches nothing, so it passes no origin, and
`2 jobs running — :jobs for details` is the whole of what it can honestly say.
The sentence itself is `components.JobsStatusLine`, shared with the workspaces
footer — two copies of a deliberate surrender would each have been free to
surrender differently.

### The activity-column guard (DEVDESK-142, A-16 skeleton)

`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go` keeps every view on the activity column
(Rule 125) and keeps it there. It classifies every `command.ViewType` into one of
two lists, **per table**: a view is migrated or exempt, never both and never
neither. There is no list of tables waiting for their story any more (DEVDESK-143
closed it) and no exception to shrink:

| List | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `migratedTables` | the view's tables are on the activity column (`:jobs`: `jobs/runs`, `jobs/targets`; ws: `ws`; `:sec`: `sec/inventory`; OCI: `oci/images`, `oci/networks`, `oci/volumes`, `oci/registries`, `oci/registry-browser`; explorer: `explorer/tree`, `explorer/clone-list`; templates: `templates`; netdiag: `netdiag/ports`; `:agent-usage`: `agent-usage/agents`; containers: `containers`) |
| `exemptViews` | views with no activity to show (dashboard, status, git-auth, configuration, about, files, viewer), each with its reason |

A view in neither list, or an exempt view that is also migrated, fails by name (`classificationProblems`, unit-tested on fictitious classifications). A migrated view
exposes `ActivityTables() map[string]datatable.ActivityTable` (a read-only face:
`Shapes()` and `RenderedWidth()`, see `ui-components.md`); an exempt view that reports any table fails with "remove the exception".

The netdiag view's `migratedSources` are two files only, `ports_model.go` and `ports_activity.go` (DEVDESK-150): netdiag migrates its Ports tab alone, and the guard scans the files that belong to it. `ports_commands.go` is left out: its `portsTickCmd` is the data refresh tick, not a row animation (same reasoning as OCI's `commands.go`). The other tabs (`forward_model.go`, checks, interfaces) are not migrated. It reports `netdiag/ports` from `ActivityTables()`, and its footer seed (`seedNetdiagFooter`) opens the Ports tab with one socket whose kill is in flight, driving the view's `Update` directly (no `Cmd` is run: no socket table read, no signal sent).

The `:agent-usage` view's `migratedSources` is the whole `ui/agentusageview/` package (no `tea.Tick` in it: `pollTickCmd` sleeps inside a `Cmd`), it reports `agent-usage/agents` from `ActivityTables()` and implements `WantsBlink()`; its footer seed (`seedAgentUsageFooter`) puts a transcript with a fresh line on disk and expects `indicator.Running`, without running the 2 s poll `Cmd`.

The templates view's `migratedSources` is the whole `ui/templates/` package; it reports `templates` from `ActivityTables()` and has a footer seed (a sync running on the selected row).

The explorer's `migratedSources` is the whole `explorer` package (no frame or `jobFrame` left in it). The explorer reports `explorer/clone-list` from `ActivityTables()` even with no clone running (same constructor), so the table is checked at 60 columns. The registry side adds `jobs.SafeCause` (credentials removed from a cause) and `jobs.CancelledDetail`.

**Checked at run time**, on each view built by the router: column 0 of every
migrated table is the indicator (untitled, fixed, `IconColumnWidth`, no `Less`,
no `Search`); `RenderedWidth()` equals `width-2` after a 60-column resize
(Rule 116); the help holds the `indicator.Legend` section.

**Checked by source analysis**, on migrated packages only (`ui/jobsview/`, `ui/workspaces/`, `ui/security/`): no
`AdvanceSpinner` call, no `StatusColumn:` key, no `Frame`/`frame`/`SpinnerFrame`
field or selector (`RenderedFrame` is allowed), no string or rune literal
holding an indicator glyph. Verified to fail on a positive case by injecting a `Frame`
field, an `AdvanceSpinner` call and a `"◉"` literal into `jobsview`.

**The footer half** is `migratedFooterSeeds` (a view seeds a row at a state and the
guard checks its footer): `:sec` is seeded by `seedSecurityFooter`, a running
scan on the selected row.

### Rule 125 : Icon column alignment

**Any icon column (or icon + short text) must be left-aligned.**

Nerd Font icons have variable width depending on the terminal. Left alignment is the only one that guarantees consistent rendering.

| Content type | Alignment |
|-----------------|------------|
| Icon alone | **Left** |
| Icon + short text | **Left** |
| Alphanumeric text | Left (default) |

#### An icon in the first column **is** a column

When a `datatable`'s first column carries a glyph, it is a column in its own
right — not a prefix stuck onto the neighboring text cell.

| | |
glyph — which stays a matter for review.

#### The activity column

**In a view with long-running operations (jobs, agents, containers), the first
column is the activity indicator.** It is built by `datatable.IndicatorColumn`,
never by a literal `Column` with an `Indicator` field set (`TestOnlyIndicatorColumnSetsIndicator`
rejects it). It keeps the icon-column shape above: untitled, `SizingFixed`,
`datatable.IconColumnWidth`. When the row is at rest (`indicator.Idle`) the
cell shows the row's own icon via its `theme.IconStyle` role, or an empty cell.

- **The color says the state, never the operation.** A scan, a clone and a
  `docker stop` that are running all look the same: `●` / `○`. What is being
  done is the footer's and the Jobs view's business.
- **No green for "done".** `Done` is `◉` in `ColorActivityNeutral`. Green stays
  reserved for the exceptions Rule 122 lists.
- **The colors are closed aliases**, assigned in `ApplyTheme`:
  `ColorActivityRunning`, `ColorActivityNeutral`, `ColorActivitySuspended`,
  `ColorActivityFailed`. They are not `icon_*` roles and no theme file gains a
  key: a theme that retuned them per state would break the one alphabet of
  states the application shares.
- **The glyph carries the meaning, the color repeats it.** Under the cursor
  the color is repainted on `ColorTableLineSelected` and the glyph still reads.
- **The blink phase is read at render.** The view's tick calls
  `m.table.SetBlinkPhase(on)`; nothing is rebuilt. Without the call the phase
  is on: a running row shows a steady `●`.

Forbidden:
- ❌ A literal `Column{Indicator: …}` instead of `datatable.IndicatorColumn`
- ❌ A glyph literal (`"●"`, `"⊗"`) in a view: use `indicator.Glyph`
- ❌ A color chosen in the view for an activity state
- ❌ Green for a finished operation
- ❌ A color that depends on the type of operation

Forbidden:
- ❌ `.Align(lipgloss.Center)` on an icon column
- ❌ `.Align(lipgloss.Right)` on an icon column
- ❌ A title above a glyph column
- ❌ A local width (`colIconFixed`, `statusColumnWidth`, a literal `2`) instead of `datatable.IconColumnWidth`
- ❌ A glyph prefixed inside a text column's cell
- ❌ An icon color chosen in the view instead of a `theme.IconStyle` role
- ❌ A color table indexed by the glyph rather than by meaning
- ❌ An icon column with no `Style`, while the other three have one
- ❌ A role per file type where the row offers the same actions

### Rule 139 : A `datatable`'s body is never replaced — not by a spinner, not by a message

**A `datatable` stays a table, whatever it contains.** Whether it is
loading its data, empty because nothing has run yet, or empty because a
filter no longer matches anything, the rendered body is always
`m.table.View()` — header included, no rows. `datatable.View()` already
does this on its own: a zero-element table renders its header and fills
the rest with the background (`internal/ui/datatable/render.go`). Nothing
in a view therefore needs to detect this case.

What a body would have said instead — loading, the row count, a verdict —
is **the footer's and header's business**, never the body's:

- loading is a `components.Status{Text: "...", Spinner: true}` in the
  footer (Rule 128);
- the row count, or whatever stands in for it (a verdict, a total), is a
  field of `GetHeaderInfo` (`shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Images", Value: "0"}`) —
  it, not the body, answers "what am I looking at."

**Why.** A body that substitutes itself for the table — with a spinner or
with text — loses its header and its columns for as long as the condition
holds, then regains them: the layout jumps on every refresh, every
`ctrl+r`, every keystroke in the filter. The header and the footer, on the
other hand, have a fixed height (Rule 124): what they display changes
without ever moving the table.

**It cannot be a `Busy func(T) bool` on the config.** Columns are built once in
`New` and close over nothing — that is why `imageRow` exists — so a predicate
there would have to close over the view's map of in-flight actions. Separating
the identity (`Key`) from the state is what avoids it, and it buys the thing
that matters most: **`IsBusy` answers for an object whose row does not exist
yet**, so it is also the guard on a confirm path. It is also what survives the
periodic refresh, which replaces the items mid-action.

A busy row is drawn by the table's `Indicator` column: `●` / `○` in that column,
the router's `jobs.FrameMsg` supplying the blink phase. The table owns no
spinner and no frame (`StatusColumn` and `AdvanceSpinner` were removed by
DEVDESK-143).

Rendering, and each part is a decision:

- The glyph shows **on the selected row too** — a signal that vanishes under
  the cursor is lost exactly when it is being looked at.
- Off the cursor every cell of the row goes `DimStyle` and the column's own
  `Style` is dropped.
- **On** the cursor the highlight itself changes
  (`theme.TableStylesForState("busy")`), overriding whatever `SelectedStyles`
  returned — a colour inside the joined row would close with a reset and end the
  highlight mid-row (`render.go`).
- The override is applied **when the row is drawn**, not when it is built, so
  the stored cells do not go stale as the phase advances. Tests assert on
  `View()`, not on `Table().Rows()`.

The activity column is the table's column 0, untitled and not sortable (Rule 125).

Every table that calls `MarkBusy` has one: `containers` (container ID; stop,
restart, pause/resume, remove), `oci` images (image ID; remove), networks
(network ID; remove), volumes (name, a volume has no ID; remove), registries
(URL; login, logout) and `netdiag` ports (PID; kill).

Two of those keys are worth the note. The ports table keys on the **PID, not the
socket**, so every row of a process shows the dot at once — which is what happens, the
kill takes them all. The registries table keys on the **URL**, which is the one
place D40's rule does not apply, and it does not apply because the *operation*
is host-scoped: one `docker login` really does change the answer for every entry
on that host.

`oci_resources` gathers `BusyLabels()` from **all four tabs**, not the active
one: an action started on Images goes on running after `tab`, and a spinner that
stopped turning because the user looked elsewhere would read as a hang on the
way back. Row state is drawn by the activity column and animated by the router's
`jobs.FrameMsg`; the view's own spinner turns only while a tab loads.

Deliberately outside this:

- **Scans** — their spinner is in the Scanned column and they do not block the
  object the same way.
- **`prune`** — it acts on no row, so marking every row would say something
  false. It gets a footer line rendered from the view's own state (`m.pruning`),
  like `syncStatusLine` (§3.17), because a footer *message* expires after three
  seconds (Rule 128) and `docker stop` outlives that by seven.
- **`workspaces`** — it already had all of this, its own way (`scanningPaths`,
  `syncingPaths`, `deletingPaths`, `busy(path)`), and is in fact where the
  design came from. Its delete was the one action its own machinery did not
  know about, and §3.23 step 1 taught it rather than migrating the view.
  Migrating would be a refactor of working code across the one busy notion that
  is *not* one object, one action: scan and sync exclude each other across
  nested paths, a sync targets a tree rather than a row, and the spinner does
  not spend the same cell for every operation.
