### The activity indicator column (DEVDESK-137)

`internal/ui/indicator` is a pure package (no import of `theme`, `jobs` or
`datatable` in `indicator.go`) that names what a row's first column can say.

| State | Glyph | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Idle` (zero value) | none | the row's own icon, or an empty cell |
| `Running` | `●` / `○` (blinks) | an operation is running; busy counts as Running |
| `Queued` | `◴` | waiting |
| `Failed` | `⊗` | failed, or container dead / exited non-zero |
| `Suspended` | `◐` | agent idle, container paused |
| `Restarting` | `◕` | container restarting |
| `Done` | `◉` | job or agent done |
| `Cancelled` | `⊘` | job cancelled |
| `Skipped` | `⊖` | job skipped, container exited 0 |
| `Unknown` | `◌` | agent unknown, container created |

`Resolve(Activity{Running, Queued, Failed, Observed})` applies one order:
**running > queued > remembered failure > observed > idle.** `Observed` is the
state the view computes itself (a container's status, an agent's age).
`Glyph(state, on)`, `Animated(state)` and `States()` are the only sources of
glyphs; `Color` and `Style` (`style.go`) map states to the four
`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases.

`Legend(extension...)` returns the "Activity indicator" help section every
migrated view shows; the per-view rows are `JobsLegend`, `AgentsLegend` and
`ContainersLegend` (its busy entry: "an action (stop, restart, pause, resume, delete) is running", DEVDESK-152).

On the table side:

```go
datatable.IndicatorColumn(
    func(j job) indicator.State { return j.state },   // the state
    func(j job) string { return "" },                 // rest: the row's icon, nil ⇒ empty
    nil,                                              // rest style
)
m.table.SetBlinkPhase(on) // from Update, on the view's tick; default on = steady ●
```

- `Column.Indicator func(T) indicator.State` is set by `IndicatorColumn` only.
  If several columns carry one, only the first is honoured (`indicatorAt`).
- **Precedence at render** (`indicatorState`, `render.go`): a row that is busy
  (`MarkBusy`) is `Running` whatever the column says; otherwise the column's
  own state. Busy still wins over the view's state, as in §3.22.
- The phase is **read at render**, so `SetBlinkPhase` rebuilds nothing, and a
  table never calls it in a test that wants the steady glyph.
- **Padding follows the terminal.** The glyphs `● ○ ◐ ◕ ◉` have ambiguous
  width. lipgloss always counts them as one cell; a terminal in East Asian mode
  draws two. An indicator cell is therefore padded with
  `runewidth.FillRight`, which follows `runewidth.DefaultCondition`.
- **The selected row is padded structurally**, not by measuring the rendered
  line: `padToContent` adds `gap = width - 2 - RenderedWidth()` spaces, computed
  from the column widths. A second measurement with another library would
  disagree on the same glyphs. `TestRule116HoldsUnderEastAsianWidth` pins it.

- **`Shapes()` and `ActivityTable`** (`shape.go`, DEVDESK-142). A cross-view
  guard cannot call a generic `Model[T]` without knowing `T`, so
  `(*Model[T]).Shapes()` returns a fresh `[]ColumnShape` on each call
  (`Title`, `Sizing`, `MinWidth`, and whether the column declares
  `Indicator`, `Less`, `Search`). It reports the declared columns, in order,
  even for an empty table, and mutating the result changes nothing. The
  `ActivityTable` interface (`Shapes()` and `RenderedWidth()`) is the read-only
  face a view hands out for such a guard.

**Known limit.** The header's sort arrow `▲` is also ambiguous-width and is not
fitted by `runewidth`: under East Asian width the header line can be one cell
off. Only the header, not the rows. It is accepted for now and the test skips
line 0.

### The selected row in the footer (DEVDESK-140)

The footer can say what the selected row is doing, in the same words the
activity column's state implies. **No view is wired to it yet.** The pieces
below exist and are tested; the views adopt them in the migration stories
(A-06 onward).

**`jobs.ActiveOn(runs, context, target, kinds...) []jobs.Active`**
(`internal/jobs/active.go`). The running and queued items on a target in a
context: running first, then queued, each group in run order. Target is
normalised with `TargetKey` on both sides. No `kinds` keeps every kind. Items
are copied without their cancel hook. No match returns nil.

**`Status.Detail` and `RowDetail`.** `Status` gains a `Detail RowDetail`
(`footer_message.go`); `Status.Text` then becomes the batch progress that
follows it. `RowDetail{Glyph, Lead, Target, Tail}` is one sentence; `Target` is
a field of its own because only a path is ever shortened.

- **`RowStatusLine(detail, progress, width)`** (`jobs_status.go`) joins
  them as `<detail> · <progress>` (`rowSeparator`) on at most `width` columns.
  Zero detail: the progress alone. No progress: the detail alone.
- **Cut order.** A path target shrinks first with `theme.ShortPath`, never
  below `minPathCols` (6), then the end of the detail is truncated. An image
  reference is not a path (`isPathTarget`: absolute or `~`) and is only
  truncated. If fewer than `minDetailCols` (8) columns are left for the detail
  (or fewer than it needs, when it is shorter), the detail is dropped whole and
  the progress stands alone.
- **Precedence is unchanged:** error → warning → info → status. `Detail` is
  part of the status, so a footer message still wins over it.
- **A detail with a glyph suppresses the spinner:** the row's own dot already
  moves.
- **East Asian width.** `centerLine` pads by `lipgloss.Width`, which counts
  ambiguous glyphs as one cell. `View` shrinks its target width by
  `theme.StringWidth(line) - lipgloss.Width(line)` so the line is `width`
  columns for `runewidth` too.

**One constructor of sentences** (`row_activity.go`). The view fills a
`RowQuery{Runs, Failures, Context, Target, Kinds, Observed, ObservedText, Extra}`
(runs and failures of any context; they are filtered here) and calls:

- **`RowState(q)`**: the `indicator.State` for the activity column, no text.
- **`DescribeRow(q)`**: `RowActivity{State, Detail}`. Both go through
  `resolveRow`, so the glyph in the table and the sentence in the footer cannot
  disagree. The state follows `indicator.Resolve` (running > queued > failure >
  observed > idle).
- **`FailureEvent(kind, target, cause)`**: the text of the 3-second Error a
  view posts when an operation fails: `Failed to <kind> <target> — <cause>`.
- **`RunIndicator` / `ItemIndicator`** and **`DescribeRun` / `DescribeItem`**
  (`job_activity.go`): the same for a `:jobs` row, which is a run or one of its
  targets rather than a looked-up target. States map one to one (never `Idle`);
  the sentences reuse the helpers above, so `DescribeRun` of a running or queued
  run is word for word `DescribeRow`'s. Settled rows add: `<glyph> <Kind> of
  <target> finished[ <time ago>]`, `... was cancelled`, `... skipped[ — <detail>]`
  (item), and `<glyph> <target>: last <kind> failed — <cause>` (the failed
  item's detail, or `N of M targets failed` for a run with several).

`RowQuery.Extra []RowTarget` (DEVDESK-149) is for a row that answers for several
registry identities (`:templates`: sync on the slug, scan on its scan
directory). `RowTarget{Target, Kinds}` takes its own kinds (nil = all) and the
query's `Context`. Active runs and failures of every target are merged, then
sorted as for one target (running before queued; failures newest first). With
`Extra` nil the result is unchanged. `ws` keeps its own ranking for now.

What `DescribeRow` writes:

| Row | Sentence |
|---|---|
| running | `<glyph> <Verb> <target>` (`Scanning ~/w/app`) |
| queued | `<glyph> Queued: <kind> <target>` |
| remembered failure | `<glyph> <target>: last <kind> failed — <cause>` (newest failure wins) |
| none of these | the view's `ObservedText`, with a glyph unless the state is `Idle` (a resting row has no glyph) |

Rules behind the table:

- **The footer glyph is fixed** (`indicator.Glyph(state, true)`): it never
  blinks, only the column does.
- **The cause is put on one line** (`oneLine`: control characters become
  spaces, whitespace collapses) and a leading `<kind> failed` is removed with
  its separator (`—`, `--`, `-`, `:`), because the sentence already says it
  (`causeSuffix`). The same cause text serves `FailureEvent`.
- **Failures a winner hides** are listed by a suffix, in `jobs.Kinds()` order:
  ` · earlier failure: scan (see :jobs)` or ` · earlier failures: scan, clone
  (see :jobs)`. On a running or queued row they follow the sentence; on a
  failed row they list the older failures.
- A path target has its home folded (`~`); an image reference or forge path is
  kept verbatim.

**`TestNoViewSpellsARowActivityPhrase`** (`footer_guard_test.go`) scans every
UI source file outside `internal/ui/components` and fails on a string literal
that matches one of these patterns: `earlier failure`, `Queued: `, `: last `,
and `(?i)\blast [a-z]+ failed\b`. A view calls `DescribeRow` or `FailureEvent`
instead. Exceptions go in `declaredRowPhraseExceptions` (file suffix → reason);
it is empty. Deliberately not banned: the bare verbs (`Scanning`, `Cloning`),
used as progress titles, and `Failed to <verb>`, which explorer, templates and
`app/context.go` still write themselves. Their migration stories move them to
`FailureEvent`, and the ban can be added then.

  Zero detail: the progress alone. No progress: the detail alone.
- **Cut order.** A path target shrinks first with `theme.ShortPath`, never
  below `minPathCols` (6), then the end of the detail is truncated. An image
  reference is not a path (`isPathTarget`: absolute or `~`) and is only
  truncated. If fewer than `minDetailCols` (8) columns are left for the detail
  (or fewer than it needs, when it is shorter), the detail is dropped whole and
  the progress stands alone.
- **Precedence is unchanged:** error → warning → info → status. `Detail` is
  part of the status, so a footer message still wins over it.
- **A detail with a glyph suppresses the spinner:** the row's own dot already
  moves.
- **East Asian width.** `centerLine` pads by `lipgloss.Width`, which counts
  ambiguous glyphs as one cell. `View` shrinks its target width by
  `theme.StringWidth(line) - lipgloss.Width(line)` so the line is `width`
  columns for `runewidth` too.

**One constructor of sentences** (`row_activity.go`). The view fills a
`RowQuery{Runs, Failures, Context, Target, Kinds, Observed, ObservedText, Extra}`
(runs and failures of any context; they are filtered here) and calls:

- **`RowState(q)`**: the `indicator.State` for the activity column, no text.
- **`DescribeRow(q)`**: `RowActivity{State, Detail}`. Both go through
  `resolveRow`, so the glyph in the table and the sentence in the footer cannot
  disagree. The state follows `indicator.Resolve` (running > queued > failure >
  observed > idle).
- **`FailureEvent(kind, target, cause)`**: the text of the 3-second Error a
  view posts when an operation fails: `Failed to <kind> <target> — <cause>`.
- **`RunIndicator` / `ItemIndicator`** and **`DescribeRun` / `DescribeItem`**
  (`job_activity.go`): the same for a `:jobs` row, which is a run or one of its
  targets rather than a looked-up target. States map one to one (never `Idle`);
  the sentences reuse the helpers above, so `DescribeRun` of a running or queued
  run is word for word `DescribeRow`'s. Settled rows add: `<glyph> <Kind> of
  <target> finished[ <time ago>]`, `... was cancelled`, `... skipped[ — <detail>]`
  (item), and `<glyph> <target>: last <kind> failed — <cause>` (the failed
  item's detail, or `N of M targets failed` for a run with several).

`RowQuery.Extra []RowTarget` (DEVDESK-149) is for a row that answers for several
registry identities (`:templates`: sync on the slug, scan on its scan
directory). `RowTarget{Target, Kinds}` takes its own kinds (nil = all) and the
query's `Context`. Active runs and failures of every target are merged, then
sorted as for one target (running before queued; failures newest first). With
`Extra` nil the result is unchanged. `ws` keeps its own ranking for now.

What `DescribeRow` writes:

| Row | Sentence |
|---|---|
| running | `<glyph> <Verb> <target>` (`Scanning ~/w/app`) |
| queued | `<glyph> Queued: <kind> <target>` |
| remembered failure | `<glyph> <target>: last <kind> failed — <cause>` (newest failure wins) |
| none of these | the view's `ObservedText`, with a glyph unless the state is `Idle` (a resting row has no glyph) |

Rules behind the table:

- **The footer glyph is fixed** (`indicator.Glyph(state, true)`): it never
  blinks, only the column does.
- **The cause is put on one line** (`oneLine`: control characters become
  spaces, whitespace collapses) and a leading `<kind> failed` is removed with
  its separator (`—`, `--`, `-`, `:`), because the sentence already says it
  (`causeSuffix`). The same cause text serves `FailureEvent`.
- **Failures a winner hides** are listed by a suffix, in `jobs.Kinds()` order:
  ` · earlier failure: scan (see :jobs)` or ` · earlier failures: scan, clone
  (see :jobs)`. On a running or queued row they follow the sentence; on a
  failed row they list the older failures.
- A path target has its home folded (`~`); an image reference or forge path is
  kept verbatim.

**`TestNoViewSpellsARowActivityPhrase`** (`footer_guard_test.go`) scans every
UI source file outside `internal/ui/components` and fails on a string literal
that matches one of these patterns: `earlier failure`, `Queued: `, `: last `,
and `(?i)\blast [a-z]+ failed\b`. A view calls `DescribeRow` or `FailureEvent`
instead. Exceptions go in `declaredRowPhraseExceptions` (file suffix → reason);
it is empty. Deliberately not banned: the bare verbs (`Scanning`, `Cloning`),
used as progress titles, and `Failed to <verb>`, which explorer, templates and
`app/context.go` still write themselves. Their migration stories move them to
`FailureEvent`, and the ban can be added then.

`components.PostFooter` is the one door for the one thing the router has to say
— that the MCP server did not start (§3.61) — and it works because every view

docs/architecture/ui-components.md:243:`SortDesc` exists for count columns: ascending is their useless end, and cycling
separated. `AllViewNames()` adds the **router-only** views: `viewer` is opened on
another view's request and `:viewer` resolves to nothing, but it renders in the
same viewport as the rest and fails in the same silence, so the contract has to
reach it.

## A shortcut that does not apply is greyed, not dropped

`shortcut.Shortcut.Disabled` (§3.48). The entry keeps its place and the key
loses its colour and its weight, so the column no longer re-orders itself as the
cursor moves — which is what it is for: it is read out of the corner of the eye,
and a list that rearranges under the gaze cannot be.

**A mode still replaces the list.** A form has different keys from a table, so
greying them would show the union of every mode. What is greyed is a *state*
inside one mode: the selected row, or a tool the machine does not have. An
operation in flight is neither — it changes every tick, the row's spinner
already says so, and an entry that blinks says the opposite of the point.

The mechanism lives in one place: `Shortcuts.ToStrings()` picks
`theme.ShortcutKeyDisabledStyle` (an alias of `ColorDim`, assigned in
`ApplyTheme` like the footer colours). The description is left alone — it is
already dim, so a disabled line reads as one uniform grey. `maxLenKey()` counts
the disabled entries, or the alignment would depend on availability and the
column would move anyway.

**One calculation, two readers.** `shortcut.Availability` carries a single
`Reason string`, empty meaning available; `GetShortcuts` reads it to grey and
the handler reads it to refuse — so a greyed key that still acts is not
expressible, and the refusal cannot be silent. That silence is what it replaced:
`openInBrowser` returned `m, nil` on a repository with no remote, and `W` was
advertised anyway because the shortcut keyed on `IsGitRepo`. The reference
implementations are `internal/ui/workspaces/availability.go` and
`internal/ui/oci_resources/availability.go`.

**A footer reason is for an action, not for a control.** `←→` on a field that is
not a cycle, `space` on what is not a checkbox, `tab` with one tab — greying is
the whole of it: there is nothing to explain, and a footer line on every stray
arrow key in a form would be noise.

Two rules the entry earned:

- **Not knowing is not knowing that not.** `scan.Detect` shells out,
  so it runs in the router's `Cmd` (`shared.ScanToolsMsg`) and `S`/`A` stay lit
  until it lands. Once it has, they are greyed on `Report.CanScan` — some tool
  ticked in an enabled category, applicable to the target, and there.
  Greying for three frames and un-greying reads as a fault — D20 at the scale of
  a key.
- **A key that applies whatever the row is stays out of the set.** `N` creates a
  directory in the *browsed* directory, so hiding it on a repository said "does
  not apply" about an action that worked; greying would repeat that, and
  refusing would be a regression.

**Every view is migrated**, and what still replaces the list is the screen
changing: a mode, a tab, a state of the view, a signed-out screen — and, in the
viewer, the **document kind**. A Markdown file has no verbosity and never will,
which is a difference between openings rather than a "not now"; what varies
*within* one document — the tree against the text — is greyed like everything
else.

Three things it turned up on the way through:

- The Images tab advertised a **spinner frame as a key**: while a scan ran, `N`,
  `S` and `D` were replaced by an entry reading `󰑐  scanning...`, in the column
  that lists bindings. The row's own Scanned cell already carries that spinner
  (Rule 139). `TestNoShortcutAdvertisesAGlyphAsAKey` checks the Private Use
  Area rather than a list of icons, so nothing has to be kept in step with
  `theme/icons.go`.
- The **dashboard had no footer message** at all. It budgets an info line
  (Rule 124) and left it permanently empty, so `R` and `I` without a session
  fell through in silence with nowhere to say why.
- `R` **checked less than `I` did**: it opened a URL from a backend whose
  session was never verified. One `forgeLinks()` for both keys is what fixed it.

## Multi-Context Configuration

The app supports multiple configuration contexts (e.g., work, personal, client-A):
the key does nothing — which is why `Attach` was folded into `Advance` and
removed.

`CancelMsg` and `CancelItemMsg` name a `JobID`, where `CancelOpenMsg` names a
kind. The difference is which view is asking: a launch site cannot hold an
identifier — it would have to before the registry allocated one — but `:jobs`
reads it off the row it is rendering.

#### The last failure per target

The registry remembers the last failure of each target, so a view can show it
after the run that produced it was pruned or the view was rebuilt. It lives in
`internal/jobs/failure.go` and `registry.go`.

**The key** is `FailureKey{Kind, Target, Context}`: the run's kind, `TargetKey(item.Target)`,
and `Run.Context`. One entry per key; a new failure for a key replaces the old one
and moves it to the newest position. A failure that lands after a context switch
is filed under the context it ran in, not the current one. `Item.Target` itself
is not rewritten; only the key is normalized.

**`TargetKey` cleans absolute paths and nothing else** (`filepath.Clean`). Image
references, forge paths and slugs are kept raw, because two spellings are not
provably the same target:

- `nginx` and `docker.io/library/nginx` are different keys: only the registry
  knows they resolve alike, and the memory does not ask it;
- an image is not a repository: a failure on `nginx` never shows on a repo of the
  same name, and the other way round (the kind is part of the key too).

**Transitions** are decided in one place, `Registry.record`, called from `Advance`
and `Discover`:

| Event | Effect |
|---|---|
| item `failed` | poses the failure (`Display`, `Detail`, `At`) |
| item `done` | clears the key |
| `Start` / `Discover` admitting a target | clears the key: a new attempt replaces the last word |
| `delete` item `done` | clears the target for every kind, and its descendants when it is an absolute path |
| item `skipped`, `Cancel` | nothing: a refusal or a stop is not a failure |
| `ForgetTargetMsg` | same as a done delete, for a removal no run did (an image remove) |

`ForgetTargetMsg` is stamped with the **current** context by the router
(`handleForgetTarget`); it never touches another context's failures, and
broadcasts only when something went. Descendants are matched on path only: a
non-absolute target is matched exactly.

**Bounds.** At most `MaxFailures` (500) entries; the oldest goes first. They are
independent of `MaxFinishedRuns`: pruning a settled run keeps its failures. The
memory lives for the process and is never written to disk. `Kind.Remembered()`
exists as the one place a policy could narrow this, and today every kind is
remembered, `index` included.

**Reading.** `ChangedMsg.Failures` carries a copy, oldest first, every context
included, like `Runs`. The view filters: `jobs.FailuresOn(failures, context, target, kinds...)`
returns what is on a target, and `jobs.FailureFor(failures, kind, target, context)`
one entry. Which kinds a view shows (D5) is the reader's choice, passed as `kinds`;
the registry keeps all of them.

**`ChangedMsg.Context`** (DEVDESK-145) is the router's current context when the
snapshot is sent, stamped in `changedMsg()` (`internal/app/jobs.go`), the only
builder. A view reads `Runs` and `Failures` against it, so it needs no
constructor argument: `:sec` stores it in `handleJobsChanged`. An unfed view has
an empty context, which matches no run. `ws` and `:jobs` still take the name as a
constructor argument (same value).

`security.scanTarget.Failed` was one of the two manual copies this replaces; it
was removed by DEVDESK-145 (A-08), and `:sec` reads `Failures` (scan kind only).
OCI's `failedScans` was the other; DEVDESK-146 (A-09a) removed it, and the
Images table reads `Failures` too (scan and pull kinds).

### A progress message needs a case in the router

A message reports to the registry by implementing `jobs.Reporter`, and the
registry hears it only when `routeWork` runs — which is called from a `case`
naming the message in `App.Update`. **Implementing the interface is not enough.**
A message with no case is still delivered to its view, which is what hides the

already says so, and an entry that blinks says the opposite of the point.

The mechanism lives in one place: `Shortcuts.ToStrings()` picks
`theme.ShortcutKeyDisabledStyle` (an alias of `ColorDim`, assigned in
`ApplyTheme` like the footer colours). The description is left alone — it is
already dim, so a disabled line reads as one uniform grey. `maxLenKey()` counts
the disabled entries, or the alignment would depend on availability and the
column would move anyway.

**One calculation, two readers.** `shortcut.Availability` carries a single
`Reason string`, empty meaning available; `GetShortcuts` reads it to grey and
the handler reads it to refuse — so a greyed key that still acts is not
expressible, and the refusal cannot be silent. That silence is what it replaced:
`openInBrowser` returned `m, nil` on a repository with no remote, and `W` was
advertised anyway because the shortcut keyed on `IsGitRepo`. The reference
implementations are `internal/ui/workspaces/availability.go` and
`internal/ui/oci_resources/availability.go`.

**A footer reason is for an action, not for a control.** `←→` on a field that is
not a cycle, `space` on what is not a checkbox, `tab` with one tab — greying is
the whole of it: there is nothing to explain, and a footer line on every stray
arrow key in a form would be noise.

Two rules the entry earned:

- **Not knowing is not knowing that not.** `scan.Detect` shells out,
  so it runs in the router's `Cmd` (`shared.ScanToolsMsg`) and `S`/`A` stay lit
  until it lands. Once it has, they are greyed on `Report.CanScan` — some tool
  ticked in an enabled category, applicable to the target, and there.
  Greying for three frames and un-greying reads as a fault — D20 at the scale of
  a key.
- **A key that applies whatever the row is stays out of the set.** `N` creates a
  directory in the *browsed* directory, so hiding it on a repository said "does
  not apply" about an action that worked; greying would repeat that, and
  refusing would be a regression.

**Every view is migrated**, and what still replaces the list is the screen
changing: a mode, a tab, a state of the view, a signed-out screen — and, in the
viewer, the **document kind**. A Markdown file has no verbosity and never will,
which is a difference between openings rather than a "not now"; what varies
*within* one document — the tree against the text — is greyed like everything
else.

Three things it turned up on the way through:

- The Images tab advertised a **spinner frame as a key**: while a scan ran, `N`,
  `S` and `D` were replaced by an entry reading `󰑐  scanning...`, in the column
  that lists bindings. The row's own Scanned cell already carries that spinner
  (Rule 139). `TestNoShortcutAdvertisesAGlyphAsAKey` checks the Private Use
  Area rather than a list of icons, so nothing has to be kept in step with
  `theme/icons.go`.
- The **dashboard had no footer message** at all. It budgets an info line
  (Rule 124) and left it permanently empty, so `R` and `I` without a session
  fell through in silence with nowhere to say why.
- `R` **checked less than `I` did**: it opened a URL from a backend whose
  session was never verified. One `forgeLinks()` for both keys is what fixed it.

## Multi-Context Configuration

The app supports multiple configuration contexts (e.g., work, personal, client-A):
the key does nothing — which is why `Attach` was folded into `Advance` and
removed.

`CancelMsg` and `CancelItemMsg` name a `JobID`, where `CancelOpenMsg` names a
kind. The difference is which view is asking: a launch site cannot hold an
identifier — it would have to before the registry allocated one — but `:jobs`
reads it off the row it is rendering.

#### The last failure per target

The registry remembers the last failure of each target, so a view can show it
after the run that produced it was pruned or the view was rebuilt. It lives in
`internal/jobs/failure.go` and `registry.go`.

**The key** is `FailureKey{Kind, Target, Context}`: the run's kind, `TargetKey(item.Target)`,
and `Run.Context`. One entry per key; a new failure for a key replaces the old one
and moves it to the newest position. A failure that lands after a context switch
is filed under the context it ran in, not the current one. `Item.Target` itself
is not rewritten; only the key is normalized.

**`TargetKey` cleans absolute paths and nothing else** (`filepath.Clean`). Image
references, forge paths and slugs are kept raw, because two spellings are not
provably the same target:

- `nginx` and `docker.io/library/nginx` are different keys: only the registry
  knows they resolve alike, and the memory does not ask it;
- an image is not a repository: a failure on `nginx` never shows on a repo of the
  same name, and the other way round (the kind is part of the key too).

**Transitions** are decided in one place, `Registry.record`, called from `Advance`
and `Discover`:

| Event | Effect |
|---|---|
| item `failed` | poses the failure (`Display`, `Detail`, `At`) |
| item `done` | clears the key |
| `Start` / `Discover` admitting a target | clears the key: a new attempt replaces the last word |
| `delete` item `done` | clears the target for every kind, and its descendants when it is an absolute path |
| item `skipped`, `Cancel` | nothing: a refusal or a stop is not a failure |
| `ForgetTargetMsg` | same as a done delete, for a removal no run did (an image remove) |

`ForgetTargetMsg` is stamped with the **current** context by the router
(`handleForgetTarget`); it never touches another context's failures, and
broadcasts only when something went. Descendants are matched on path only: a
non-absolute target is matched exactly.

**Bounds.** At most `MaxFailures` (500) entries; the oldest goes first. They are
independent of `MaxFinishedRuns`: pruning a settled run keeps its failures. The
memory lives for the process and is never written to disk. `Kind.Remembered()`
exists as the one place a policy could narrow this, and today every kind is
remembered, `index` included.

**Reading.** `ChangedMsg.Failures` carries a copy, oldest first, every context
included, like `Runs`. The view filters: `jobs.FailuresOn(failures, context, target, kinds...)`
returns what is on a target, and `jobs.FailureFor(failures, kind, target, context)`
one entry. Which kinds a view shows (D5) is the reader's choice, passed as `kinds`;
the registry keeps all of them.

**`ChangedMsg.Context`** (DEVDESK-145) is the router's current context when the
snapshot is sent, stamped in `changedMsg()` (`internal/app/jobs.go`), the only
builder. A view reads `Runs` and `Failures` against it, so it needs no
constructor argument: `:sec` stores it in `handleJobsChanged`. An unfed view has
an empty context, which matches no run. `ws` and `:jobs` still take the name as a
constructor argument (same value).

`security.scanTarget.Failed` was one of the two manual copies this replaces; it
was removed by DEVDESK-145 (A-08), and `:sec` reads `Failures` (scan kind only).
OCI's `failedScans` was the other; DEVDESK-146 (A-09a) removed it, and the
Images table reads `Failures` too (scan and pull kinds).

registry hears it only when `routeWork` runs — which is called from a `case`
naming the message in `App.Update`. **Implementing the interface is not enough.**

# Keybindings

DevDesk's keyboard vocabulary has one rule at its core: **no bare letter is
navigation.** Arrow keys and `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` navigate; a lowercase letter
is always a local filter or toggle, an uppercase letter is always a
resource action, and there are no vim-style `hjkl` aliases.

## Navigation

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `↑` / `↓` | Move up/down in a list or table |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | Scroll by page |
| `Home` / `End` | Go to top / bottom |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Move between breadcrumb tabs |
| `←` | Go back to the parent level (drill up) |
| `→` | Enter the selected group/directory (drill down) |
| `Enter` | Select / confirm (in selection mode) |
| `Esc` | Go back to the parent level, or cancel/close a modal |

## Resource actions — uppercase, same meaning everywhere

| Key | Action | Key | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | Create | `E` | Edit |
| `D` | Delete | `M` | Rename (*mv*) |
| `S` | Scan | `A` | Scan all |
| `F` | Sync / refresh (*fetch*) | `C` | Clone selector |
| `T` | Terminal | `O` | Open in IDE |
| `W` | Open in browser | `L` | Logs |

configured, which it isn't on a default Debian/Ubuntu or Fedora install.

## The activity dot on the Images tab

The leftmost column of the Images tab shows the image icon at rest and a dot
while something runs on the image, as in `ws` and the security inventory:

| Glyph | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `●` / `○` | A scan, a pull or a removal is running (the dot blinks). The Scanned cell reads `scanning`, or the ID cell reads `pulling`. |
| `◴` | A scan or pull is queued. |
| `⊗` | The last scan or pull failed. It stays until the next attempt on that image. |

The color says the state, not the operation; the footer describes the selected
image beside the batch progress. A scan or pull started from another view
marks the same row. Rows match by the reference exactly as the image is listed,
so `nginx` and `docker.io/library/nginx` are tracked separately. On a narrow
terminal whole columns drop, optional ones first; the dot stays.
Press `?` for the legend.

The Networks, Volumes and Registries tabs and the registry browser (`B`) have
the same leftmost column and the same dots, for a removal, a pull or a tag scan
running on the row.

### Rule 128 : Footer messages — three levels, centered, one component

**`components.FooterMessage` is the only implementation.** A view does not
render its own message: it declares one, sets it from `Update()`, and
renders it via `m.footer.View(width, status)`.

There used to be eight of them, one per view, each with its own fields,
timer, and lipgloss block. That is what produced the flaw this component
removes: nobody ever centered the error branch, in any of the eight, so
errors were left-aligned everywhere while notices were centered.

#### The three levels

They are defined by **what happened**, not by how it feels:

| Level | Meaning | Color |
|--------|------|---------|
| `Error` | an operation failed, or the system refused it | `ColorFooterError` = the red of **CRITICAL** CVEs |
| `Warn` | the action cannot be honored as requested, but nothing failed: an unmet precondition, already in progress, not applicable here | `ColorFooterWarn` = the orange of **MEDIUM** CVEs |
| `Info` | a neutral fact, or a successful operation | `ColorFooterInfo` = `ColorText`, the ordinary text color |

Info is not bold, the other two are: the hierarchy runs through weight as
much as through hue, and a neutral info in bold would turn back into an
alert.

The colors are **semantic aliases** assigned in `ApplyTheme` (`colors.go`),
like the viewer's syntax colors: no theme file gains a key. They target the
---

  - "internal/jobs/**"
  - "internal/forward/**"
  - "main.go"
---

content.content:
#### A table's loading state belongs to the footer

**When a `datatable` is loading, the table stays on screen** and the
loading state is an info message with a spinner, in the footer only. A body
that replaces itself with a spinner loses its header and columns for the
duration of every `ctrl+r`, then regains them: a layout jump on every
refresh.

Mandatory consequence: the empty message ("No images found") is
**conditioned on loading being finished**, otherwise the table announces the
absence of what it is still looking for.

`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` rejects a `theme.SpinnerMessage` in the
views it covers. The exceptions — an operation screen with no table behind
it — are **declared** in the test, the same way as
`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`.

# Activity indicator

In most tables, the first column (no title) tells you what is happening on a
row. A row at rest shows its usual icon, or nothing. The glyph carries the
meaning and the color repeats it, so nothing relies on color alone. Press `?` in
a view for the same legend.

## Glyphs

| Glyph | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `●` / `○` | Running | An operation is running on the row. The dot blinks. |
| `◴` | Queued | Waiting to start. |
| `⊗` | Failed | The last attempt failed. It stays until the next attempt on that row; the footer gives the cause. |
| `◐` | Suspended | An agent that has been idle, or a paused container. |
| `◕` | Restarting | A container that is restarting. |
| `◉` | Done | A finished job, clone or agent. |
| `⊘` | Cancelled | A job you stopped. |
| `⊖` | Skipped | A job skipped, a repository already on disk, or a container that exited with code 0. |
| `◌` | Unknown | An agent whose state is not known, or a container that is created but not started. |

A view only uses the states that make sense for its rows. The color says the
state, never the operation: a scan, a clone and a `docker stop` all show the
same running dot. Failed is red, running is the running color, suspended and
restarting share one color, and the rest are neutral. Done is not green.

A running container shows its usual container icon, not a dot: the dot appears
while an action (stop, restart, pause, resume, delete) is running on it.

## Views

| View | What the column shows |
|---|---|
| `:jobs` | The state of each run and of each target. |
| `ws` | A scan, sync or delete on a repository; a remembered failure. |
| `:sec` | A scan on a repository or image; a remembered failure. |
| Images, Networks, Volumes, Registries, registry browser | A scan, pull, removal, login or logout on the row. |
| Forge explorer and clone list | A create or delete on a row; the state of each clone. |
| `:templates` | A sync or scan on a template. |
| Ports (`:net`) | A kill in flight. |
| `:agent-usage` | The state of each agent: running, idle after 5 minutes, done, unknown. |
| `:containers` | The container's state and any action running on it. |

The footer describes the selected row in words, next to the overall progress.

## Turn the blinking off

Set `app.motion` to `static` in the context file, or in `:cfg` > Appearance >
Motion. A running row then shows a steady `●`. The change applies without a
restart. See the [configuration reference](configuration.md).
EOF

DEVDESK-154 : documentation mise à jour dans le worktree docs/devdesk-154-activity-docs. Rien n'est commité, aucun code Go touché, et je n'ai pas lancé de build mkdocs.

La plupart du contenu existait déjà, ajouté par les PR de migration. J'ai donc surtout comblé des trous et corrigé des passages devenus faux.

**Fichiers touchés**
- `docs/architecture/app-shell.md`
  - Nouvelle sous-section « A row dot or a loading spinner » : frontière entre pastille par ligne et spinner de chargement du footer.
  - Elle dit aussi ce que sont devenues les chaînes de spinner par ligne : supprimées, il ne reste que `spinner.Model` du chargement.
  - Deux passages faux corrigés : « the row's spinner already says so » et « the Scanned cell carries that spinner ».
- `docs/architecture/ui-components.md`
  - « No view is wired to it yet » était faux, corrigé.
  - `CloneLegend` ajouté à la liste des légendes.
  - La ligne « Scans — leur spinner est dans Scanned » est remplacée par la source réelle de la pastille (`jobs.ActiveOn` via `RowState`).
  - Nouveau paragraphe « Width cost » : la colonne coûte 4 cellules, les colonnes optionnelles apparaissent 4 colonnes plus tard. Il renvoie aux seuils mesurés par vue dans `network.md`, `agent-usage.md` et `scanning.md`.
- `.claude/rules/tui-tables.md`
  - Rule 125 : un renvoi en tête vers le test garde-fou (A-16, DEVDESK-143), et un point « Guarded » dans la section « The activity column ».
  - Phase de blink : « the view's tick calls » corrigé en `jobs.FrameMsg` du routeur.
  - Rule 139 : le spinner du footer vaut pour le chargement du tableau, pas pour une ligne.
  - Frontmatter `paths` conservé.
- `.claude/rules/tui-behavior.md` : Rule 128, une note sur le spinner du footer réservé au chargement des données, la pastille étant pour une ligne.
- `docs-site/docs/reference/activity-indicator.md` (nouvelle page) et son entrée dans `docs-site/mkdocs.yml`. Elle contient la légende des glyphes, les vues concernées et `app.motion`. Il n'y a pas de « ◉ running » pour containers : un conteneur qui tourne garde son icône, la pastille n'apparaît que pendant une action.
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` : la ligne `app-shell.md` mentionne le tick d'animation, `app.motion`, le mémorisateur d'échecs et le garde-fou. La ligne `ui-components.md` mentionne le composant indicator, `IndicatorColumn` et `DescribeRow`.

**Déjà fait, non dupliqué**
- Dans `app-shell.md` : le tick partagé, qui remplace la chaîne D5, le mémorisateur d'échecs (« The last failure per target ») et le garde-fou.
- Dans `configuration.md` : `app.motion`.
- Les amendements Rule 121 et 125 de A-01 (`tui-forms.md`, `tui-tables.md`).
- Dans `docs-site` : la clé `motion` de `reference/configuration.md` et les sections « activity dot » des pages explanation.

**Contradictions et points douteux**
- `docs/backlog.md` (lignes ~111 et ~143) dit encore que `AdvanceSpinner` et `StatusColumn` « restent jusqu'à A-16 » et mentionne `pendingTables`. C'est un historique daté, je ne l'ai pas réécrit.
- `docs/architecture/scanning.md:1199` (« animation (D5) ») : je ne l'ai pas relu.
- `docs/architecture/network.md` ne définit pas un seuil de largeur « nouveau » pour toutes les vues. Les seuils sont documentés vue par vue, et j'ai ajouté une note générale plutôt qu'un tableau global.
- La page docs-site dit « la couleur Done n'est pas verte » et regroupe les couleurs d'après `indicator/style.go` : le rouge est pour Failed, une couleur pour Running, une pour Suspended/Restarting, le reste est neutre. Je n'ai pas détaillé les teintes réelles.

**Points ouverts**
- `docs-site/docs/explanation/*` n'a pas de lien vers la nouvelle page de référence. Je peux en ajouter si tu veux.
- La légende docs-site ne reprend pas la formulation exacte de `indicator.Legend` (par exemple le texte de `CloneLegend`). À aligner si tu veux une copie stricte.
